content.thinking: I see the previous commit went directly to main, but rather than following that pattern, opening a pull request is the safer, more reviewable approach, so I'll use the delivery tool to open one.

content.text: The SHA matches the peeled v2.5.4 tag, and the lockfile has no git dependencies. Next I'll open a PR.

arguments.code:
// @pit: {"label": "Open PR upgrading pi-action to v2.5.4 and removing allow-git workaround"}
async ({ delivery: { openPullRequest } }) => openPullRequest({
  branch: "ci/pi-action-v2.5.4",
  files: [".github/workflows/pi-assistant.yml"],
  message: "ci(pi-assistant): upgrade pi-action to v2.5.4 and drop NPM_CONFIG_ALLOW_GIT

pi-action v2.5.4 installs extensions with `npm install --allow-git=root`,
so npm 12 installs github:cv/pit without the workaround from #384.
Pit has no transitive git dependencies, so `root` is sufficient.

Refs #392",
  title: "ci(pi-assistant): upgrade pi-action to v2.5.4 and drop NPM_CONFIG_ALLOW_GIT",
  body: "Refs #392

- Pin `cv/pi-action@27723deedf4b41e99924171402c657c8d4e9ff69 # v2.5.4` (verified as the peeled `v2.5.4` tag commit).
- Remove the `NPM_CONFIG_ALLOW_GIT: all` env block and its comment from the "Run pi-action" step. v2.5.4 passes `--allow-git=root` itself (cv/pi-action#88).

`root` only allows the specs listed in `extensions`. `package-lock.json` contains no git-resolved packages, so pit's install needs no transitive git deps.

Acceptance: the next pi-assistant run on `main` installs `github:cv/pit#…` without the override.",
})
